requirements.req_text: Do the following: (a) Explain to your counselor the most likely hazards you may encounter while hiking, and what you should do to anticipate, help prevent, mitigate, and respond to these hazards. (b) Show that you know first aid for injuries or illnesses that could occur while hiking, including hypothermia, frostbite, dehydration, heat exhaustion, heatstroke, sunburn, hyperventilation, altitude sickness, sprained ankle, blisters, insect stings, tick bites, and snakebite.

People Wholose Water: People wholose more water than they take in risk becoming dehydrated.
Sign Dehydration Dark: The first sign of dehydration usually is dark urine.
Signscan Include Weariness: Other signscan include weariness, headache, body aches, and confusion.
step_by_step_procedure: Heat Exhaustion Heatstroke: Heat exhaustion, heatstroke, and hypothermia might all becaused in part by dehydration.
Prevent Dehydration Heat: Prevent dehydration and heat reactions by drinking plentyof fluids.
Easy Hot Summer: That is easy to do on hot summer days when you arethirsty.

pamphlet_excerpts: Caring Environment: Caring for the environment is an important responsibility ofevery hiker.
Leave Trace Principles: Leave No Trace is just one set of principles that canhelp you live up to that responsibility and enjoy the outdoorsfully by knowing that you.
Group Plan Hike: As you and your group plan a hike, ask yourselves how youcan follow each of the principles of Leave No Trace.
Leave Trace Outdoor: Leave No Trace and The Outdoor Code are principles that help yourespect the environment and be considerate to others who areenjoying the outdoors.
step_by_step_procedure: Explain Desired Route: Explain your desired route and askhow you can best implement Leave No Trace.
Here Someadditional: Here are someadditional guidelines to remember.
Remember this solid guideline: Pack it in, pack it out.
Easier Yourself Limitingthe: Make it easier on yourself by limitingthe amount of potential trash you take.

pamphlet_excerpts: Setting Off Hike: Setting off on a hike without properly preparing can havedisastrous results.
Ready Yourphysical Condition: Make sure you are ready, from yourphysical condition to the best gear for the trip.
Want Goodshape: To enjoy hiking to the fullest, you will want to be in goodshape.
Requirement Calls Developing: That is why requirement 3 calls for developing a planfor conditioning yourself.
step_by_step_procedure: Begin Short Trips: Begin with short trips, increasingthe length of your journeys as you become more fit.
Goodway Prepare Hikes: A goodway to prepare for Scout hikes is to walk when­ever you canrather than riding in a car or relying on public transit.
Word Aerobic Means: The word aerobic means “with oxygen.” Aerobic activitiesincrease the rate of your breathing and your heartbeat, andpush your body to use oxygen more.
Aerobic Trainingcan: Aerobic trainingcan strengthen your circula­tory and respiratory systems, add mass to muscles and bones, burn excess fat, and lead toimprovements.

requirements.lead_text: Take four 10-mile hikes and one 20-mile hike, each on a different day, and each of continuous miles. Prepare a written hike plan before each hike and share it with your counselor or a designee for approval before starting the hike. Include map routes, a clothing and equipment list, and a list of items for a trail lunch. You may stop for as many short rest periods as needed, as well as one meal, during each hike, but not for an extended period such as overnight.
requirements.req_text: Take four 10-mile hikes and one 20-mile hike, each on a different day, and each of continuous miles. Prepare a written hike plan before each hike and share it with your counselor or a designee for approval before starting the hike. Include map routes, a clothing and equipment list, and a list of items for a trail lunch. You may stop for as many short rest periods as needed, as well as one meal, during each hike, but not for an extended period such as overnight. pamphlet_excerpts: Mile Hike Twenty: Go! 20-Mile Hike Twenty miles is a long way, but with the hiking you’ve done sofar, you will be ready.
Mark Map Placesyou: Mark on a map any placesyou can cut your trip short if weather, weariness, or injuriessurprise you along the way.
Breakfast Early Start: Have a good breakfast and get an early start so that youcan finish your hike before dark.
Carry Extra Socks: Carry extra socks that you canchange into during the day.
step_by_step_procedure: Pack Plenty High-energy: Pack plenty of high-energy foodsboth for your lunch as well as for trail snacks throughout theday.
Plan Adequate Water: Be sure to plan for an adequate water supply for the trail.
Opportunityto Explore: Get the most you can from every opportunityto explore the outdoors.
There Adventure Than: There is no better adventure than heading out with your friends to discover the freedom of the trail.

requirements.lead_text: After each of the hikes (or during each hike if on one continuous trek) in requirement 4, write a short report on your hike. For each hike, give the date and description (or map) of the route covered, the weather, any interesting things you saw, and any challenges you had and how you overcame them. It may include something you learned about yourself, about the outdoors, or about others you were hiking with. Share this with your counselor.

pamphlet_excerpts: Mile Hike Twenty: Go! 20-Mile Hike Twenty miles is a long way, but with the hiking you’ve done sofar, you will be ready.
Mark Map Placesyou: Mark on a map any placesyou can cut your trip short if weather, weariness, or injuriessurprise you along the way.
Breakfast Early Start: Have a good breakfast and get an early start so that youcan finish your hike before dark.
Carry Extra Socks: Carry extra socks that you canchange into during the day.
step_by_step_procedure: Pack Plenty High-energy: Pack plenty of high-energy foodsboth for your lunch as well as for trail snacks throughout theday.
Plan Adequate Water: Be sure to plan for an adequate water supply for the trail.
Opportunityto Explore: Get the most you can from every opportunityto explore the outdoors.
There Adventure Than: There is no better adventure than heading out with your friends to discover the freedom of the trail.
